assessment.overall_rationale: The sets strongly preserve the detoxification and lipid-homeostasis programs, while the candidate redistributes bile-acid sulfation and Cdo1-mediated sulfur metabolism into a combined bile-acid module and leaves nitrogen disposal without a close counterpart.

pair_scores.rationale: Both describe the same pericentral hepatic Phase I/II detoxification battery, although the right module omits the left module's prominent SULT-mediated steroid and bile-acid conjugation arm.

They share the specific SULT2A-mediated bile-acid sulfation mechanism, but the left centers broad xenobiotic detoxification whereas the right combines sulfation with Cdo1-dependent taurine production.
Their overlap is limited to aldehyde and lipid-derived metabolite handling within hepatic metabolism, while their central outputs are detoxification versus lipid storage and oxidation.
Aldh3a2 links lipid oxidation to reactive-aldehyde detoxification, but the modules principally concern lipid flux and organelle metabolism versus xenobiotic defense.
Both contribute broadly to hepatic lipid and sterol homeostasis and reference Abcg5, but bile-acid conjugation is peripheral to the left module's lipid-droplet and peroxisomal oxidation mechanism.
Both center FITM1-dependent lipid-droplet formation and ECI2/HAO2-dependent peroxisomal fatty-acid oxidation, with the right adding a polyol-fructose metabolic branch.
Both are liver metabolic programs, but nitrogen and sulfur-amino-acid disposal is mechanistically distinct from Phase I/II xenobiotic detoxification.
They share the central Cdo1-mediated conversion of cysteine toward taurine, but the left emphasizes amino-acid and ammonia disposal while the right emphasizes bile-acid conjugation and sulfation.
The modules share only a broad hepatic metabolic context, with amino-acid nitrogen disposal unrelated to lipid-droplet, fatty-acid oxidation, and polyol metabolism.
